seed: Objects of type `marker` under action ACTION3 with touching neighbours [hazard,wall] show mixed outcomes: gone x2, no_change x2. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: state accumulated across earlier steps that the frame does not show. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Blocks (colour 10, 4x4) move as a pair: A1 up, A2 down, A3 apart, A4 together; each moves only if its destination 4x4 is all floor colour 5.
Clicking a colour-9 marker arms it: blocks become colour 1, the marker becomes 11, the old active marker reverts to 9. Clicking a colour-1 player disarms. While armed, A1-A4 move the active marker cell under the same floor rule. A5 = no-op.
HUD: colour-0 bars on row 0 (right-aligned) and row 63 (left-aligned), width 3(a+1)//7, a = actions this level. a is hidden, carried across calls only when the frame matches the last one returned; otherwise it falls back to the largest a that fits the bar.
Hypothesis: the marker A3 gone/no_change split is object renaming when the bar first appears, plus floor-colour blocking. The only hidden accumulated state is the action counter.
Unconfirmed: what happens when a bar reaches full width; clicking non-marker cells is treated as a no-op.
